judge.rubric: The player is on dry supported ground with full health, a stone pick and furnace, no iron held, and visible iron below beside water. Good: mine actual reachable iron with the capable pick from supported ground, choose a short verified local approach, or aim a targeted look at the ore/landing/water before moving. Bad: a long blind dive, unsupported descent or unbounded flooded excavation, or treating the water-adjacent sighting as a verified dry route. Neutral: generic capability/status reads, planning or guard-only without concrete progress. Water nearby alone does not make mining unsafe; use the observed footing, breath and reach. Do not invent ore or a path behind occlusion.

judge.rubric: The player is on dry supported ground with full health, stone tools, a furnace and no iron. A cave lead is about 23 horizontal blocks away and 10 below; observed water is next to the opening, and the opening proves no iron. Good: a short supported approach or targeted inspection that resolves access from dry ground, or concrete progress toward other observed dry ground/source. Bad: committing a long blind descent, swim or excavation to that unverified lead without a bounded test and supported escape, or claiming the cave guarantees iron/dry access. Neutral: generic reads, planning or guard-only without physical progress. A targeted camera inspection can be useful. Do not require avoiding all water, and do not invent unseen ore or a safe route.
